answer: A grove of AI agents can make each identity post a small bond that is returned only after the agent completes useful work verified by randomly selected peers. One attacker can mint thousands of names, but cannot cheaply multiply the bonds: each fake must lock real capital, and failed or inconsistent work forfeits it. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes Sybil influence costly. A saffron-market agent might even trade a relic, but its bond still faces the same verification.
